content.user_title: Plan Content Strategies That Drive Demand
content.value_statement: Teams often choose content topics without clear buyer intent or distribution value. This skill builds content pillars, topic clusters, and prioritized ideas from customer, search, and competitor inputs.
actual_capabilities: Creates three to five content pillars aligned to product goals and audience needs.
Maps topic clusters with hub, spoke, and internal linking recommendations.
Classifies topics by buyer stage, search intent, and content type.
Prioritizes content ideas using customer impact, content-market fit, search potential, and resources.
Extracts content ideas from keyword exports, calls, surveys, forums, competitors, and support input.
Recommends searchable and shareable content formats for each strategy.
limitations: It depends on the quality of customer, keyword, and competitor inputs provided by the user.
It does not perform technical SEO audits or on-page optimization checks.
It does not write full articles, landing pages, or social posts by itself.
It cannot verify live search volume or competitor rankings without current data supplied or web access.

use_cases.title: Build a SaaS Editorial Roadmap
use_cases.description: Turn customer problems, product use cases, and competitor gaps into a quarterly topic plan.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Topics From Research
use_cases.description: Rank ideas from call transcripts, surveys, support tickets, and keyword exports with clear scoring criteria.

use_cases.title: Create Authority Topic Clusters
use_cases.description: Define pillars, subtopics, and internal linking paths for a focused content library.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Content Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning from basic business context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a content strategy for my business. Ask only for missing details about our audience, goals, product, competitors, and existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Research Into Topics
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these customer notes, survey responses, and support themes. Extract content ideas, buyer stages, pain points, and supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Map Pillars and Clusters
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced structure for an authority-building content library.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build three to five content pillars for this product. Include cluster topics, hub or blog structure, internal linking logic, and product alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Content Backlog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced roadmap scoring for resource planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score this content backlog by customer impact, content-market fit, search potential, and resource requirements. Return a prioritized roadmap with rationale.

output_examples.input: We sell project management software for agencies and need blog topics for next quarter.
output: Three pillars: client collaboration, agency operations, and project visibility.
Priority topic: project management for creative agencies, mapped to consideration stage.
Recommended format: use-case article with product-led examples and links to related templates.

output_examples.input: Here are support ticket themes about onboarding, permissions, and reporting confusion.
output: Implementation-stage cluster: setup guides, permission tutorials, reporting examples, and troubleshooting articles.
Customer impact is high because the same themes appear across onboarding and support.
Suggested next asset: step-by-step reporting setup tutorial with common mistakes addressed.

output_examples.input: Our competitors rank for broad guides, but their posts lack customer examples.
output: Opportunity: create comparison and guide content with original customer scenarios.
Shareable angle: lessons from real implementation patterns across customer segments.
Searchable angle: target long-tail comparison and template queries.

best_practices: Provide customer language, sales questions, support themes, and keyword exports before asking for a roadmap.
Tie each content pillar to a product use case and a measurable business goal.
Review topic priorities against available writers, subject experts, and distribution channels.
anti_patterns: Do not request a topic list without audience, product, and goal context.
Do not treat search volume as the only priority signal for content planning.
Do not build complex hub pages when simple blog posts and internal links are enough.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces content pillars, topic clusters, prioritized topics, and research-backed rationale for a content strategy.

faq.question: Can it use keyword research exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze provided exports for clusters, intent, buyer stage, quick wins, and content gaps.

faq.question: Does it replace an SEO audit?
faq.answer: No. It supports content planning. Technical SEO and on-page audits should use a dedicated SEO workflow.

faq.question: Can it plan both searchable and shareable content?
faq.answer: Yes. It separates demand-capture content from demand-creation content and explains when to use each type.

faq.question: What inputs improve the results?
faq.answer: Customer calls, support tickets, surveys, competitor examples, keyword data, product positioning, and current content performance improve results.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for small teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend simpler blog structures and prioritize topics against limited writing time and budget.
